t.4.52.1: Thus addressed by the female ascetic with auspicious words in accord with dharma, Hanumān spoke these words to her whose conduct was beyond reproach.
t.4.52.3: Therefore you should lead us out of this terrible cave.
t.4.52.2: We have all come to you for refuge, O you who walk in dharma. The time limit that the great-souled Sugrīva set for us has already passed, so let it now go by here in the cave.
t.4.52.5: O you who walk in dharma, a great task must be accomplished by us, and yet that task has not been done by us while dwelling here.
t.4.52.4: You ought to save all of us, who have overstepped that command of Sugrīva, whose lives are as good as gone, and who are filled with dread out of fear of Sugrīva.
t.4.52.6: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the female ascetic spoke these words: "I think it is hard for one who has entered here to return alive."
t.4.52.7: But by the power of my austerity, acquired through religious discipline, I shall lift all the monkeys out of this cave.
t.4.52.8: Close your eyes, all of you, O bulls among the vānaras; for it is not possible to get out with eyes unclosed.
t.4.52.9: Then all of them, their eyes closed, joyful and eager to depart, at once covered their sight with hands of delicate fingers.
t.4.52.10: Then the great-souled monkeys, their faces covered with their hands, were brought out of the cave by her in no more than the twinkling of an eye.
t.4.52.11: Then the female ascetic, devoted to dharma, having comforted all those monkeys who had come out of that perilous place, spoke these words.
t.4.52.12: This is the glorious Vindhya mountain, covered with many kinds of trees and creepers; this is the Prasravaṇa mountain, and this is the ocean, the great reservoir of waters.
t.4.52.13: "May it be well with you, O bulls among the monkeys; I shall go to my dwelling." Having spoken thus, Svayaṃprabhā entered that splendid cave.
t.4.52.14: Then they beheld the terrible ocean, the abode of Varuṇa, boundless and roaring, agitated by fearsome waves.
t.4.52.15: While they were searching the mountain fortress fashioned by the magic of Maya, the month that the king had set as the appointed time passed by.
t.4.52.16: Then, seated at the foot of Mount Vindhya, where the trees were in full bloom, those illustrious ones fell into anxious thought.
t.4.52.17: Then, seeing the trees of springtime, their crowns weighed down by an excessive burden of blossoms and enveloped by hundreds of creepers, they became filled with fear and misgiving.
t.4.52.19: Then that monkey, the crown prince Aṅgada, of great wisdom, with shoulders like those of a lion or a bull and with stout, long arms, spoke these words.
t.4.52.18: Telling one another that spring had arrived, they, whose purpose within the time set by the command had now been lost, fell down upon the surface of the earth.
t.4.52.20: By the command of the king of the monkeys we all set out; a month has passed for us dwelling in this cave, O monkeys, is this not understood?
t.4.52.21: But now that the time fixed by Sugrīva himself has passed, fasting unto death is the fitting course for all of us forest-dwellers.
t.4.52.23: And if there is no news of Sītā, he will surely do us harm. Therefore it is fitting for us to undertake the fast unto death right here, this very day.
t.4.52.22: Sugrīva is harsh by nature and is now firmly established in the position of master; he will not forgive any of us, who have gone back to him as offenders.
t.4.52.24: We have left behind our sons and wives, our wealth and our homes; rather than have the king put all of us to death by an unworthy execution when we return from here, it is better that we die right here.
t.4.52.25: And it was not Sugrīva who had me consecrated as crown prince; I was consecrated by Rāma, lord of men, whose deeds are untiring.
t.4.52.26: That king, who has long harbored enmity toward me, will, on seeing my transgression, resolutely have me put to death with a harsh punishment.
t.4.52.28: Having heard this, spoken by the young prince, the heir-apparent, all those foremost of monkeys uttered piteous words.
t.4.52.27: What use are friends to me, who would only look upon my misfortune at the close of my life? Right here, on the sacred shore of the ocean, I shall sit and fast unto death.
t.4.52.29: Sugrīva is fierce by nature, and Rāghava is devoted to his beloved; and when, Vaidehī not having been found, they see us returned together...
t.4.52.31: Having heard the words of the monkeys, who were tormented by fear, Tāra spoke thus: "Enough of despair! Let us all enter the cave and dwell there, if it pleases you."
t.4.52.30: Wishing to do what is dear to Rāghava, he will without doubt have us put to death; and it is not fitting for those who have failed in their duty to go back to their master's side.
t.4.52.32: For this place, fashioned by magic, is very hard to reach and abounds in trees, water, food and drink; here we have no fear at all, not from Puraṃdara, nor from Rāghava, nor even from the king of the monkeys.
t.4.52.33: Having heard Aṅgada's agreeable words, all the monkeys, reassured, said: “Let a plan be devised for us, without delay, this very day, such that we may not be slain.”
